Ask Culture and Guess Culture

Within the Western world, males are more likely to be operating under an Ask culture and Females are more likely to be operating under a Guess culture (article). In Ask culture, the attitude is that it is always okay to ask, because the other person can always say no. In Guess culture, the attitude is that you shouldn't put someone under pressure and that simply forming a request will often do that. This means that you are expected to have a good idea of whether or not they are likely to say yes before phrasing your request. The difficultly comes about because some people are raised more in an Ask culture and some more in a Guess culture.

Males adopt more of an Ask Culture because directness and assertiveness are qualities that society values in males. In contrast, society expects females to be nice. Saying things too directly is often considered a Faux Pas for females. This forces them to develop a more indirect style of communication.

Dominance of male view points within the mainstream media

Films, books and TV shows are predominately written by males. The statistics for female TV writers might not seem that bad compared to the other two - 30% are female - but keep in mind that a large percentage of those female writers work for TV shows aimed towards the female market and that the percentage of female writers on shows that males actually watch is likely to be much lower.

The result is that women are exposed much more to the male point of view, then men are exposed to the female point of view. Even when their is a female protagonist, it is often written by a man who has simply mapped their understanding of men onto women. In contrast, a female writer can produce a convincing male character simply by basing it on how all the other male characters appear.

So while women will generally pick up some basic understanding of male points of view from mass media, men often will not have been exposed to these viewpoints enough to develop a strong understanding. (It pays to note that although women will generally have picked up a basic understanding, some will labour under the delusion that TV and movie have taught them everything that they need to know about the opposite sex).

Difference blindness

There are some people, who whenever you want to talk about gender differences, will loudly proclaim that there are no differences. Perhaps you believe that there aren't any significant biological differences in terms of behavior, but to claim that there are no cultural differences between men and women requires a stunning level of ignorance. Some people are genuine, but if you were to meet them in another context you will usually find such attitudes as, "Why are teenage boys so immature?", "I bet we wouldn't have all these wars if women were in charge", and so forth.

Unfortunately, some people buy this hook, line and sinker. They believe that there aren't any cultural or behavioural differences between men and women, so they don't look for them, so they don't understand women. The worst aspect is that often these people won't even realise that they don't understand women.

No-one would deny that the Chinese and Egyptians have different cultures, similarly, it is just as boring to state that men and women have different cultures.
